offense_class: Class D Crime (first/second); Class C Crime (third+)
elements: Defendant operated or attempted to operate a motor vehicle
While under the influence of intoxicants
Or with a BAC of .08 or higher
mandatory_minimum: 48 hours or 2 days (first with BAC .15+); 7 days (second); 30 days (third)
enhancements: Exceeding speed limit by 30+ mph while OUI
notes: Maine uses 'OUI' (Operating Under the Influence). Implied consent under 29-A M.R.S. § 2521. License suspension 150 days first offense. Lookback period is 10 years.

offense_class: Class D Crime
elements: Defendant operated or attempted to operate a motor vehicle
While under the influence of intoxicants or with BAC .08+
No prior OUI convictions within 10 years
mandatory_minimum: 48 hours if BAC .15 or higher; otherwise no mandatory jail
notes: 150-day license suspension. $500 minimum fine. Eligible for alternative sentencing programs.

offense_class: Class D Crime (second); Class C Crime (third+)
elements: Defendant operated or attempted to operate a motor vehicle
While under the influence of intoxicants or with BAC .08+
One or more prior OUI convictions within 10 years
enhancements: Fourth or subsequent offense (Class C Crime with 6-month mandatory minimum)
notes: Second offense: 3-year license suspension. Third+: 6-year suspension. Ignition interlock required for reinstatement.

offense_class: Same as alcohol OUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol OUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol OUI by offense count
elements: Defendant operated or attempted to operate a motor vehicle
While under the influence of a drug or combination of drugs
Or the combined influence of intoxicants and drugs
To a degree that impairs the defendant's ability to operate safely
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol OUI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of drugs and alcohol
notes: No per se drug limit in Maine. Prosecution relies on drug recognition expert (DRE) evaluations and behavioral evidence.

offense_class: Class E Crime
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle
In a manner that created a substantial risk of serious bodily injury to another person
notes: Common plea-down from OUI. 30-day license suspension upon conviction.

statute_title: Leaving Scene of Accident — Injury or Death
offense_class: Class C Crime (injury/death); Class E Crime (property damage under § 2253)
elements: Defendant was the operator of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to stop and remain at the scene
Defendant failed to provide name, address, and registration
notes: Leaving scene involving death or serious injury is a Class C Crime. Property damage only is a Class E Crime.

offense_class: Class A Crime
elements: Defendant recklessly or with criminal negligence caused the death of another person
While operating a motor vehicle
enhancements: Operating under the influence at the time
notes: Maine does not have a separate vehicular homicide statute. Vehicular deaths are charged under manslaughter (§ 203) or criminal OUI causing death (29-A M.R.S. § 2411(6)).

offense_class: Class D Crime (first); Class C Crime (subsequent)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
License was under suspension or revocation
Defendant had knowledge or notice of the suspension
notes: Operating after OUI suspension carries mandatory jail time. Non-OUI suspension under § 2412 is a Class E Crime with lesser penalties.

offense_class: Class C Crime
elements: A law enforcement officer gave a visual or audible signal to stop
Defendant was aware of the signal
Defendant failed to stop
Defendant attempted to elude the officer by driving recklessly
enhancements: Creating a substantial risk of serious bodily injury
notes: Officer must be in uniform or identifiable law enforcement vehicle. License revocation upon conviction.

offense_class: Class D Crime (most); Class C Crime (large amounts)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed a scheduled drug
Drug is listed in 17-A M.R.S. §§ 1101–1106
Possession was without valid prescription
enhancements: Possession of certain quantities triggers trafficking charges
notes: Maine decriminalized small amounts of marijuana (up to 2.5 oz for adults 21+). Scheduled drug possession remains criminal.

offense_class: Civil Violation (up to 2.5 oz); Class E Crime (over 2.5 oz)
penalty_max: Civil fine (up to 2.5 oz); 6 months (over 2.5 oz criminal)
elements: Defendant possessed marijuana
Defendant was 21 years of age or older
Amount exceeded legal limits or defendant was under 21
notes: Maine legalized recreational marijuana for adults 21+ in 2016 (up to 2.5 oz). Amounts over 2.5 oz or possession by persons under 21 remain criminal.

offense_class: Class D Crime (under 2g); Class C Crime (2g or more)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Schedule W substance in Maine
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: Cocaine is classified as a Schedule W drug in Maine. Larger quantities may support trafficking charges.

offense_class: Class D Crime (under 2g); Class C Crime (2g or more)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Schedule W substance
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: Methamphetamine is classified as a Schedule W drug. Maine has seen increasing meth-related charges in recent years.

offense_class: Class A Crime (Schedule W); Class B Crime (other schedules)
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly trafficked in a scheduled drug
Trafficking includes manufacturing, distributing, or possessing with intent to distribute
Aggravating factors present (quantity, location, prior convictions)
enhancements: Use of a firearm during the offense
notes: Aggravated trafficking is Maine's most serious drug offense. Separate from unlawful trafficking under § 1105-C.

offense_class: Class B Crime (Schedule W); Class C Crime (other schedules)
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly trafficked in a scheduled drug
Trafficking includes furnishing, selling, or possessing with intent to furnish
notes: Lower-level trafficking offense compared to aggravated trafficking. Covers sale and distribution without aggravating factors.

offense_class: Class B Crime
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly manufactured a scheduled drug
Manufacturing includes producing, preparing, or compounding
enhancements: Manufacturing near a school or in presence of a child
notes: Manufacturing methamphetamine carries additional penalties. Environmental cleanup costs may also be assessed.

offense_class: Civil Violation (personal use); Class D Crime (sale/delivery)
elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia
With knowledge that it would be used for scheduled drugs
enhancements: Sale or delivery of paraphernalia to a minor
notes: Personal use possession is a civil violation. Sale or delivery of paraphernalia is a Class D Crime.

statute_title: Possession with Intent to Furnish — Scheduled Drugs
offense_class: Class B Crime (Schedule W); Class C Crime (other schedules)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a scheduled drug
With intent to furnish or distribute the drug
notes: Intent to distribute is inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, large amounts of cash, and other indicators.

offense_class: Class A Crime (Murder is unclassified; 25 years to life)
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused the death of another person
Or engaged in conduct that manifested a depraved indifference to human life and created a grave risk of death
enhancements: Victim was a law enforcement officer
notes: Maine abolished the death penalty in 1887. Murder carries a mandatory minimum of 25 years. Maine does not distinguish between first and second degree murder by statute — all intentional killings are 'murder' under § 152.

offense_class: Class A Crime
elements: Defendant recklessly or with criminal negligence caused the death of another person
Under circumstances that would otherwise be murder but for adequate provocation or extreme emotional disturbance
notes: Maine treats manslaughter as a single offense under § 203. Provocation or emotional disturbance reduces murder to manslaughter.

offense_class: Class A Crime
elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Through criminal negligence
notes: Criminally negligent homicide that does not rise to recklessness. Same statutory section as reckless manslaughter.

offense_class: Class B Crime (general); Class A Crime (serious bodily injury with dangerous weapon)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused serious bodily injury to another person
Or caused bodily injury with a dangerous weapon
enhancements: Use of a dangerous weapon (Class A)
Victim is a law enforcement officer
Victim is under 6 years of age
notes: Serious bodily injury means substantial risk of death, unconsciousness, extreme physical pain, protracted disfigurement, or loss of bodily function.

offense_class: Class D Crime
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to another person
Or intentionally or knowingly caused physical contact of an insulting or provoking nature
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer (Class C Crime under § 207-A)
notes: Maine does not have a separate battery statute. Assault covers both threats and physical contact.

offense_class: Class B Crime
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to another
With a dangerous weapon
enhancements: Serious bodily injury results (Class A Crime)
Victim is a law enforcement officer
notes: Dangerous weapon includes firearms, knives, and any other object used in a manner likely to produce death or serious bodily injury.

offense_class: Class A Crime
elements: Defendant committed or attempted to commit theft
Used force, threatened use of force, or placed the victim in fear of force
Force was used to overcome resistance, compel compliance, or prevent resistance
enhancements: Displayed what appeared to be a firearm
notes: All robbery in Maine is a Class A Crime regardless of whether a weapon was used. The weapon or injury affects sentencing.

offense_class: Class A Crime
elements: Defendant committed or attempted to commit theft
Was armed with a dangerous weapon during the commission of the crime
Used or threatened force
notes: Armed robbery is the most serious robbery charge. No separate statute — charged under the general robbery statute with weapon enhancement.

offense_class: Class A Crime
elements: Defendant knowingly restrained another person
With the intent to hold for ransom, use as a shield or hostage, inflict bodily injury, terrorize, or interfere with government function
enhancements: Victim was held for more than 12 hours
notes: Criminal restraint (§ 302) is a lesser included offense. Kidnapping requires specific intent beyond mere restraint.

offense_class: Class A Crime
elements: Defendant started, caused, or maintained a fire or explosion
On the property of another
Thereby recklessly endangering the life of any person
enhancements: Fire set in an occupied structure
notes: Arson of occupied structures is the most severely punished. Causing a catastrophe (§ 803) is a related offense.

offense_class: Class A Crime
elements: Defendant took a substantial step toward intentionally or knowingly causing the death of another person
With the intent to commit murder
enhancements: Victim was a law enforcement officer
notes: Attempted murder is charged under the attempt statute (§ 153) in conjunction with the murder statute (§ 152). Carries the same class as the completed offense.

statute_title: Theft by Unauthorized Taking or Transfer
offense_class: Class E Crime (under $1,000); Class C Crime ($1,000–$10,000); Class B Crime ($10,000+)
penalty_max: 6 months (Class E); 5 years (Class C); 10 years (Class B)
elements: Defendant obtained or exercised unauthorized control over the property of another
With intent to deprive the owner of the property
enhancements: Theft from a person (Class C minimum)
notes: Maine consolidated theft offenses under Title 17-A Chapter 15. Value thresholds determine the crime classification.

offense_class: Class C Crime ($1,000–$10,000); Class B Crime ($10,000+)
elements: Defendant obtained or exercised unauthorized control over the property of another
Value of property exceeded $1,000
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Maine does not use the term 'grand theft' — this corresponds to theft where value exceeds $1,000.

offense_class: Class E Crime
elements: Defendant obtained or exercised unauthorized control over the property of another
Value of property was under $1,000
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Class E Crime. Shoplifting may be charged under § 357 (theft of services) or this general theft provision.

offense_class: Class E Crime (under $1,000); Class C Crime ($1,000+)
elements: Defendant obtained or exercised control over retail merchandise
With intent to deprive the owner without paying full value
notes: Shoplifting is generally charged as theft by unauthorized taking (§ 353) or theft by deception (§ 354).

offense_class: Class B Crime (general); Class A Crime (armed or dangerous weapon)
elements: Defendant entered or surreptitiously remained in a structure
Knowing entry was not licensed or privileged
With intent to commit a crime therein
enhancements: Armed with a dangerous weapon (Class A Crime)
Structure was a dwelling (Class A Crime)
Caused or attempted to cause bodily injury
notes: Burglary of a dwelling or while armed is elevated to Class A Crime. Nighttime burglary also carries heavier sentencing.

offense_class: Class A Crime
elements: Defendant entered or remained unlawfully in a dwelling
Knowing entry was not licensed or privileged
With intent to commit a crime therein
notes: A 'dwelling' is any structure used for overnight accommodation. Elevated to Class A Crime regardless of time of day.

offense_class: Class C Crime (most vehicles); Class B Crime ($10,000+)
elements: Defendant obtained or exercised unauthorized control over a motor vehicle
With intent to deprive the owner
enhancements: Vehicle used in commission of another crime
notes: No separate motor vehicle theft statute. Charged under general theft with classification based on vehicle value.

offense_class: Same class as corresponding theft offense
penalty_max: Up to 10 years depending on value
elements: Defendant received, retained, or disposed of stolen property
Knowing that it was stolen or believing it was probably stolen
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Classified at the same level as the corresponding theft offense based on value of property received.

offense_class: Class D Crime (under $2,000); Class C Crime ($2,000+)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly damaged or destroyed property of another
enhancements: Damage to a public utility or infrastructure
notes: Maine uses 'criminal mischief' rather than 'vandalism.' Graffiti and property destruction fall under this statute.

offense_class: Class E Crime (general); Class D Crime (dwelling)
elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained in a place
Without license or privilege to do so
After having been forbidden to enter or having been ordered to leave
enhancements: Trespass in a dwelling (Class D Crime)
notes: Criminal trespass in a dwelling carries heavier penalties than trespass on other property.

offense_class: Class D Crime (general); Class C Crime (damage $2,000+)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly damaged or destroyed the property of another
Or tampered with property creating risk of harm
notes: Covers property damage, tampering, and destruction. Value of damage determines crime classification.

offense_class: Class D Crime (first); Class C Crime (prior conviction within 10 years)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to a family or household member
Family or household member includes current/former spouse, cohabitant, parent of common child
enhancements: Prior DV conviction within 10 years (Class C Crime)
notes: Maine has mandatory arrest policy for DV crimes. Second offense within 10 years is elevated. Firearms prohibition upon conviction.

offense_class: Class D Crime
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused physical contact with a family or household member
Contact was of an insulting or provoking nature
notes: Maine does not have a separate battery statute. Domestic violence offenses are covered under § 207-A.

statute_title: Endangering the Welfare of a Child
offense_class: Class D Crime (general); Class C Crime (substantial risk of serious harm)
elements: Defendant knowingly permitted a child to enter or remain in a situation that endangered the child's health or welfare
enhancements: Substantial risk of serious harm (Class C Crime)
notes: Covers a range of conduct including leaving a child unattended, exposing a child to drugs, or failing to provide necessities.

statute_title: Domestic Violence Assault — Against a Minor
offense_class: Class D Crime (general); Class B Crime (serious bodily injury)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to a child
Child is a family or household member
enhancements: Serious bodily injury (elevated to aggravated assault under § 208)
notes: Child abuse may be charged under DV assault (§ 207-A) or aggravated assault (§ 208) depending on severity. DHHS involvement mandatory.

offense_class: Class D Crime (first); Class C Crime (subsequent)
elements: A valid protection from abuse order was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant intentionally violated a condition of the order
enhancements: Violation involved assault or threatening conduct
notes: Mandatory arrest for violations. Second or subsequent violation is a Class C Crime.

offense_class: Class D Crime (general); Class C Crime (aggravated under § 210-B)
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly engaged in a course of conduct directed at a specific person
That would cause a reasonable person to suffer serious inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm
Conduct occurred on two or more occasions
enhancements: Violation of a protective order (Class C Crime)
notes: Aggravated stalking (§ 210-B) is a Class C Crime. Includes cyberstalking.

offense_class: Class D Crime (general); Class E Crime (telephone/electronic harassment)
elements: Defendant engaged in conduct directed at a specific person
With intent to harass, torment, or threaten
After being warned to cease
enhancements: Harassment by telephone or electronic device
notes: Includes telephone harassment and cyberbullying. Repeated unwanted contact after warning constitutes harassment.

statute_title: Endangering the Welfare of a Dependent Person
offense_class: Class D Crime (general); Class C Crime (serious risk of harm)
elements: Defendant was a caretaker of a dependent person
Defendant knowingly endangered the health, safety, or welfare of the dependent person
notes: Covers elderly, disabled, and other dependent persons. Financial exploitation is charged under § 174-B.

statute_title: Possession of Firearms by Prohibited Persons
offense_class: Class D Crime (general); Class C Crime (certain prohibited persons)
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant was a prohibited person under federal or state law
Including persons convicted of certain crimes or subject to protective orders
notes: Maine is a constitutional carry state — no permit needed for most adults. Prohibited persons include felons, persons under protective orders, and certain others.

offense_class: Class C Crime
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant had been convicted of a crime punishable by one year or more of imprisonment
enhancements: Possession during commission of another crime
notes: Federal charges under 18 U.S.C. § 922(g) may also apply. Restoration of firearms rights available after certain waiting periods.

offense_class: Class E Crime
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
In a location where firearms are prohibited by law
Including courthouses, schools, and federal buildings
notes: Maine adopted constitutional carry in 2015. No permit required for most adults 21+. Restrictions remain for prohibited locations.

offense_class: Class C Crime
elements: Defendant recklessly created a substantial risk of serious bodily injury
By discharging a firearm
notes: Charged as reckless conduct under Maine law. Municipalities may have additional discharge ordinances.

offense_class: Class D Crime (general); Class C Crime (financial harm $10,000+)
elements: Defendant knowingly used personal identifying information of another person
Without that person's consent
With intent to obtain a benefit or cause harm
notes: Includes use of Social Security numbers, credit card numbers, and other personal identifying information.

offense_class: Classified by value same as theft
penalty_max: Up to 10 years depending on value
elements: Defendant obtained property of another that had been entrusted to the defendant
Defendant dealt with the property in a manner contrary to the terms of the entrustment
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Charged under theft by misapplication. Value determines crime classification.

offense_class: Class C Crime (general); Class B Crime (currency, securities, stamps)
elements: Defendant falsely made, completed, or altered a written instrument
With intent to defraud or deceive
enhancements: Forgery of currency or government documents (Class B)
notes: Includes forging checks, documents, and identification. Aggravated forgery of currency is a Class B Crime.

offense_class: Class B Crime
elements: Defendant forged or uttered a forged instrument
Instrument was currency, stamps, securities, or government-issued documents
notes: Federal counterfeiting charges may also apply under 18 U.S.C. § 471.

offense_class: Class E Crime (under $500); Class D Crime ($500–$1,000); Class C Crime ($1,000+)
penalty_max: 6 months (Class E); 364 days (Class D); 5 years (Class C)
elements: Defendant issued or negotiated a check or similar instrument
Knowing there were insufficient funds to cover it
With intent to defraud
notes: Defendant must have had knowledge of insufficient funds at time of issuance.

offense_class: Class C Crime (most); Class B Crime ($10,000+)
elements: Defendant submitted a false insurance claim
With intent to obtain insurance proceeds by deception
notes: Charged as theft by deception under general theft statutes. Restitution typically ordered.

offense_class: Class D Crime (general); Class C Crime (value $1,000+)
elements: Defendant used a credit card, debit card, or similar device
Knowing it was stolen, forged, expired, or revoked
With intent to defraud
notes: Includes unauthorized use of credit cards, debit cards, and electronic payment methods.

offense_class: Class B Crime
elements: Defendant conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction
Knowing the transaction involved proceeds of criminal activity
With intent to conceal the source or nature of the proceeds
notes: Federal money laundering charges under 18 U.S.C. § 1956 may also apply.

offense_class: Classified by value same as theft
penalty_max: Up to 10 years depending on value
elements: Defendant obtained property or services through deception
By creating a false impression, preventing another from acquiring relevant information, or failing to disclose a known lien
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: General fraud is prosecuted under the theft by deception statute. Classification depends on the value obtained.

offense_class: Class A Crime (most); Class B Crime (certain circumstances)
elements: Defendant engaged in a sexual act with another person
By compulsion or against the will of the other person
Or the other person was incapable of consent due to intoxication, disability, or age
notes: Maine uses 'gross sexual assault' rather than 'rape.' Class A Crime when compulsion is used or victim is under 14.

offense_class: Class A Crime
elements: Defendant engaged in a sexual act with another person
Through compulsion by use of physical force or threat of physical force
Or the other person was physically helpless
notes: Maine does not use the term 'rape' in its statutes. This offense is 'gross sexual assault' under § 253.

offense_class: Class E Crime (general); Class D Crime (prior conviction or victim under 12)
elements: Defendant, in a public place, exposed genitals
Under circumstances that the defendant should know are likely to cause affront or alarm
notes: Maine uses 'indecent conduct' rather than 'indecent exposure.' Sex offender registration may be required for repeat offenders.

offense_class: Class D Crime (first); Class C Crime (subsequent)
elements: Defendant engaged or agreed to engage in a sexual act
In exchange for a pecuniary benefit
notes: Maine focuses enforcement on buyers. Promoting prostitution (§ 852) is a separate, more serious offense.

offense_class: Class B Crime (general); Class A Crime (dissemination)
elements: Defendant knowingly employed, used, or permitted a minor to engage in sexually explicit conduct
For the purpose of producing visual depictions
notes: Includes production, distribution, and possession of child sexual abuse material. Federal charges under 18 U.S.C. § 2251 may also apply.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender
offense_class: Class D Crime (first); Class C Crime (subsequent)
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender
Defendant knowingly failed to register or update registration information
notes: Maine Sex Offender Registration and Notification Act. Registration for 10 years or lifetime depending on offense.

offense_class: Class C Crime (victim 14-15); Class B Crime (victim under 14)
elements: Defendant engaged in a sexual act with a person under 16
Defendant was at least 5 years older than the victim (victim 14-15)
Or at least 3 years older (victim under 14)
enhancements: Defendant in a position of authority
notes: Age of consent in Maine is 16. Close-in-age exceptions apply. Sex offender registration required upon conviction.

offense_class: Class E Crime
elements: Defendant, in a public place, intentionally or recklessly caused annoyance to others
By engaging in fighting, violent, or threatening behavior
Or by creating a hazardous or physically offensive condition
notes: Lowest-level public order offense. Often charged alongside other offenses or as a plea-down.

statute_title: Refusing to Submit to Arrest or Detention
offense_class: Class D Crime (general); Class C Crime (if injury to officer)
elements: A law enforcement officer attempted to make a lawful arrest or detention
Defendant intentionally or knowingly refused to submit
By using or threatening to use physical force
enhancements: Causing bodily injury to the officer (Class C)
notes: Passive resistance (going limp) generally does not constitute this offense. Must involve physical force or threat of force.

offense_class: Class D Crime (general); Class C Crime (physical force involved)
elements: Defendant intentionally obstructed, impaired, or hindered the performance of a governmental function
By use of force, violence, physical interference, or obstacle
notes: Covers interference with any government function, not limited to law enforcement.

offense_class: Civil or Criminal Contempt
elements: A valid court order was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant willfully disobeyed or violated the order
notes: Civil contempt is coercive — defendant can purge by compliance. Criminal contempt is punitive.

offense_class: Class E Crime
elements: Defendant appeared in a public place while intoxicated
Defendant's conduct was disorderly or created a hazardous condition
notes: Maine does not have a standalone public intoxication statute. Intoxication-related public behavior is charged under disorderly conduct.

offense_class: Class E Crime (if underlying was Class D/E); Class C Crime (if underlying was Class A/B/C)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or personal recognizance
Defendant was required to appear in court
Defendant knowingly failed to appear as required
enhancements: Underlying charge was a serious felony (Class C)
notes: Classification of failure to appear depends on the classification of the underlying charge.

offense_class: Class D Crime (general); Class C Crime (bomb threat or causing evacuation)
elements: Defendant knowingly gave a false report to law enforcement
Or initiated a false alarm
Report or alarm related to a crime, emergency, or hazardous condition
enhancements: Report caused emergency response or evacuation (Class C)
notes: Includes filing false police reports, making bomb threats, and initiating false fire alarms.

offense_class: Class D Crime (general); Class C Crime (with dangerous weapon or terroristic threats)
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly placed another person in fear of imminent bodily injury
By physical conduct or words
enhancements: Display of a dangerous weapon (Class C)
Threat of death or serious bodily injury (Class C)
Threat directed at a school or public building
notes: Terroristic threatening (§ 210) is a separate, more serious offense involving threats to cause catastrophe.

offense_class: Class C Crime
elements: Defendant made a false statement under oath
In an official proceeding
Knowing the statement was false
Statement was material to the proceeding
notes: Includes testimony in court proceedings, depositions, and sworn affidavits.

offense_class: Class B Crime
elements: Defendant offered, conferred, or agreed to confer a benefit
Upon a public servant
With intent to influence the public servant's official action
notes: Covers both offering and receiving bribes. Separate offense for bribery of witnesses under § 454.

offense_class: Class C Crime (from jail/prison); Class D Crime (from custody/supervision)
elements: Defendant was in official custody or detention
Defendant intentionally escaped or attempted to escape
notes: Includes escape from jails, prisons, and court-ordered supervision. Walking away from work release may qualify.

offense_class: Class D Crime (general); Class C Crime (aggravated)
penalty_max: 364 days (Class D); 5 years (Class C aggravated under § 1031(1-C))
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused cruel treatment to an animal
Including torture, overworking, abandonment, or failure to provide necessities
enhancements: Aggravated cruelty (torture causing extreme physical pain, Class C)
notes: Aggravated animal cruelty (§ 1031(1-C)) is a Class C Crime. Court may order forfeiture of animals and prohibition on future ownership.

offense_class: Same class as underlying offense
penalty_max: Up to the maximum of the original sentence
elements: Defendant was on probation for a criminal conviction
Defendant violated a condition of probation
Violation was inexcusable
enhancements: Committing a new crime while on probation
notes: Court may revoke probation and impose any sentence that could have been imposed originally. Graduated sanctions may apply.

offense_class: Administrative (revocation to prison)
elements: Defendant was on supervised community confinement or supervised release
Defendant violated a condition of supervision
notes: Maine uses supervised community confinement rather than traditional parole. Violations may result in return to prison for the balance of the sentence.

statute_title: Criminal Liability for Conduct of Another
offense_class: Same as the principal offense
elements: Defendant aided, agreed to aid, or attempted to aid another person
In the planning or commission of a crime
With the intent to promote or facilitate the crime
notes: Accomplice liability in Maine. An aider carries the same criminal liability as the person who directly committed the crime.

offense_class: One class below the target offense (Class B if target is Class A, etc.)
penalty_max: One grade below the completed offense
fine_max: One grade below the completed offense
elements: Defendant intentionally engaged in conduct that constituted a substantial step toward commission of a crime
Defendant had the intent to commit the crime
notes: Attempt is generally classified one grade below the target offense. Attempted murder remains Class A.

offense_class: One class below the target offense
penalty_max: One grade below the completed offense
fine_max: One grade below the completed offense
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons to commit a crime
Defendant or a co-conspirator performed an overt act in furtherance of the conspiracy
notes: Conspiracy is classified one grade below the target offense. An overt act by any co-conspirator is sufficient.

statute_title: Aggravated Sex Trafficking / Trafficking in Persons
offense_class: Class A Crime (sex trafficking); Class B Crime (labor trafficking)
elements: Defendant knowingly recruited, enticed, harbored, transported, or obtained another person
Through force, fraud, or coercion
For the purpose of commercial sexual activity or forced labor
notes: Maine enacted comprehensive anti-trafficking legislation. Victims are not prosecuted for crimes committed under trafficking coercion.

offense_class: Class D Crime
elements: Defendant knowingly restrained another person
Restraint was without consent and substantially interfered with the person's liberty
enhancements: Restrained in conditions creating serious risk of harm
notes: Criminal restraint is a lesser included offense of kidnapping. Does not require specific intent beyond the restraint itself.

offense_class: Class D Crime (under 2g); Class C Crime (2g or more)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed an opioid drug
Including heroin, fentanyl, or oxycodone without prescription
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: Maine's opioid crisis has led to increased enforcement. Fentanyl-related cases carry heightened attention from prosecutors.
